Field-by-field description of every definition kind, the argument grammars the `add*` and `set*` functions accept, and the plot-configuration support matrices.

Each table's **If omitted** column is the one to read when you are deciding what you actually have to supply: it says whether a field falls back to a default, is taken from the model file as exported from PK-Sim or MoBi, or simply does not apply.

Two conventions run through all of it:

- Every `add*`, `set*`, and `remove*` function takes `project` first and the definition's `id` second. Only the fields after those are listed below.
- Every `add*` function accepts `overwrite`, a logical defaulting to `FALSE`. An id that already exists aborts unless you pass `overwrite = TRUE`, which replaces the definition (last write wins). It is omitted from the tables. The one carve-out is `addObservedData()`: `overwrite = TRUE` replaces a source only when the new one is the same kind as the old, and a cross-kind replacement is refused in either direction whatever you pass, so remove the existing source with `removeObservedData()` first.

For why definitions are shaped this way, see `vignette("about-the-project-model")` and `vignette("about-the-plotting-model")`. For the project file and folder layout, see `vignette("reference-project-file")`.

## Scenario

`addScenario(project, id, modelFile, ...)`. Only `modelFile` is required.

| Field | Required | Type | If omitted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelFile` | **yes** | string | Aborts. Named relative to the project's simulations folder. |
| `individual` | no | id | The model's own individual is simulated, as exported from PK-Sim or MoBi. |
| `population` | no | id | The scenario is an individual scenario. Supplying one makes it a population simulation. |
| `application` | no | id | The dosing in the model file is used unchanged. |
| `parameterSets` | no | character vector of ids | No parameter sets are layered on; the model's own values apply. |
| `initialConditions` | no | character vector of ids | The model's own initial conditions apply. |
| `outputPaths` | no | character vector of ids | The output selections stored in the model file are recorded. |
| `simulationTime` | no | interval string or numeric | The time grid stored in the model file is used. |
| `simulationTimeUnit` | no | string | `"h"`. |
| `steadyState` | no | logical | `FALSE`, so no steady-state pre-run. |
| `steadyStateTime` | no | numeric | `1000`. |
| `steadyStateTimeUnit` | no | string | `"min"`. |
| `overwriteFormulasInSS` | no | logical | `FALSE`. |
| `readPopulationFromCSV` | no | logical | `FALSE`. |
| `solverSettings` | no | named list | The project's `defaultSolverSettings` apply, and for a setting the project does not give, the value stored in the model file. |

Two behaviors are not visible from the table:

- **Every reference is checked as the scenario is added.** If `individual`, `population`, `application`, or any entry in `parameterSets`, `initialConditions`, or `outputPaths` does not resolve, `addScenario()` aborts and nothing is created. The model file is not checked then; `validateProject()` warns when it is missing.
- **Parameter sets are applied in layers.** First the scenario's own `parameterSets`, in the order you list them, then the parameter sets of its individual, then those of its application. Where two sets touch the same parameter, the one applied last wins: `c("global", "aciclovir", "ckd")` applies `global` first and lets `ckd` win, and a set of the individual or the application overrides all three.

### Scenario files

**A `definitions/scenarios/*.json` file uses the argument names above**, unchanged, and so does a scenario record read from `project$definitions$scenarios`. So a scenario file written by hand looks like this:

```json
{
  "id": "aciclovir_iv",
  "modelFile": "Aciclovir.pkml",
  "individual": "adult_male",
  "application": "aciclovir_iv_250mg",
  "parameterSets": ["global", "aciclovir"],
  "outputPaths": ["aciclovir_pvb"],
  "steadyState": false
}
```

The record also carries `simulationType`, derived from whether a population is referenced.

### `solverSettings`

How the solver behaves for this scenario, as a named list of [`SolverSettings`](https://www.open-systems-pharmacology.org/OSPSuite-R/reference/SolverSettings.html) values. Give only the ones you want to change:

```r
addScenario(project, "stiff_iv",
  modelFile = "Aciclovir.pkml",
  solverSettings = list(relTol = 1e-6, checkForNegativeValues = FALSE)
)
```

| Setting | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `absTol` | number | Absolute tolerance. |
| `relTol` | number | Relative tolerance. |
| `h0` | number | Initial step size. |
| `hMin` | number | Smallest step size the solver may take. |
| `hMax` | number | Largest step size the solver may take. |
| `mxStep` | whole number | Maximum number of internal steps per output interval. |
| `useJacobian` | logical | Whether the analytic Jacobian is used. |
| `checkForNegativeValues` | logical | Whether the solver checks for negative values. |

A setting given here wins over the project's `defaultSolverSettings`, and the `solverSettings` argument of `runScenarios()` or `buildSimulations()` wins over both. A setting you leave out keeps the project's value, or the value stored in the model file where the project gives none. `setScenario()` replaces the whole block rather than merging into it, so pass every setting you want kept, and `solverSettings = NULL` clears it. See `vignette("reference-project-file")` for the full chain.

### `simulationTime` grammar

A string of one or more intervals. One interval is `"start, end, resolution"`, where resolution is the number of points per unit of `simulationTimeUnit`. Several intervals are separated by `;`:

```r
simulationTime = "0, 24, 60"            # 24 hours, 60 points per hour
simulationTime = "0, 20, 60; 20, 504, 1" # dense first 20 h, coarse tail
```

A single interval may also be given as a numeric vector `c(start, end, resolution)`. The stored form is always a list of length-3 numeric vectors, one per interval.

## Individual

`addIndividual(project, id, species, ...)`. Only `species` is required.

| Field | Required | Type | If omitted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `species` | **yes** | string | Aborts. |
| `gender` | no | `GenderInt` token | `"UNKNOWN"`, which is the only valid PK-Sim gender for some animal species. A supplied value must be a valid token. |
| `population` | no | string | Not set; PK-Sim uses its own default. |
| `weight` | no | numeric | Taken from the PK-Sim individual for the species and demographics. |
| `height` | no | numeric | Taken from the PK-Sim individual. |
| `age` | no | numeric | Taken from the PK-Sim individual. |
| `proteinOntogenies` | no | character vector of `"Protein:Ontogeny"` | No ontogenies applied. The ontogeny name must be a key of `ospsuite::StandardOntogeny`, checked when the scenario runs. |
| `parameterSets` | no | character vector of ids | No individual-specific parameter sets. Validated at add time. |

`proteinOntogenies` also accepts the same pairs as one comma-joined string, which is how the Excel sheets spell it. Numeric fields are coerced with `as.double()`.

`setIndividual(project, id, ...)` changes named fields on an existing individual and accepts the same set.

## Population

`addPopulation(project, id, species, numberOfIndividuals = NULL, ...)`.

A population is either a **demographics spec** (the default, no `type` field) or a **source**, set by `type`:

| `type` | Meaning | Required field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| absent | Demographics spec to sample | `species` |
| `"csv"` | Read from a population CSV | `file` |
| `"programmatic"` | A `Population` object held in the session | none |

Fields of a demographics spec:

| Field | Required | Type | If omitted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `species` | **yes** | string | Aborts. |
| `numberOfIndividuals` | no | numeric | Not set. Must be positive when supplied. |
| `proportionOfFemales` | no | numeric | Not constrained. A value outside 0 to 100 warns. |
| `ageMin`, `ageMax` | no | numeric | Unconstrained. |
| `weightMin`, `weightMax` | no | numeric | Unconstrained. |
| `heightMin`, `heightMax` | no | numeric | Unconstrained. |
| `BMIMin`, `BMIMax` | no | numeric | Unconstrained. |
| `ageUnit`, `weightUnit`, `heightUnit`, `BMIUnit` | no | string | PK-Sim defaults. |
| `gender` | no | string | Not set. |
| `population` | no | string | PK-Sim default. |
| `diseaseState` | no | string | Healthy. |
| `proteinOntogenies` | no | character vector | No ontogenies applied. |

A `csv` population must name its `file`; omitting it is a validation error, not a fallback.

The `<id>.csv` derivation belongs to a different mechanism: a scenario carrying `readPopulationFromCSV = TRUE`, which looks for `<id>.csv` in the populations folder. That lookup is case-insensitive against the folder listing, with an exact match winning, because an id is lowercase while a CSV keeps the case its author gave it.

## Application

`addApplication(project, id, parameterSets = NULL)`.

| Field | Required | Type | If omitted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `parameterSets` | no | character vector of ids | The application carries no dosing parameters of its own. |

An application is a thin record: the dose, start time, and other administration parameters live in the parameter sets it references.

## Parameter set

Two functions. `addParameterSet(project, id)` creates an empty set; `addParameterEntry(project, id, containerPath, parameterName, value, units = NULL)` fills it. One call can add several entries: give each field as a vector with one element per entry, all of the same length.

| Field | Required | Type | If omitted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `containerPath` | **yes** | non-empty strings, one per entry | Aborts. |
| `parameterName` | **yes** | non-empty strings, one per entry | Aborts. |
| `value` | **yes** | numbers, one per entry | Aborts. |
| `units` | no | strings, one per entry | The value is taken to be in the parameter's base unit. Use `""` for a dimensionless parameter. |

`containerPath` is the container in OSPS path notation. `addParameterEntry()` creates the set on demand if it does not yet exist. A repeated `(containerPath, parameterName)` pair **aborts** unless you pass `overwrite = TRUE`, which replaces the existing entry (last write wins), so building a set incrementally does not silently overwrite what is already there. `removeParameterEntry()` takes an entry back out and auto-removes the set if it becomes empty; `removeParameterSet()` drops a whole set.

Scenarios, individuals and applications all reference parameter sets from this one collection by id.

## Initial conditions

`addInitialConditions(project, id)` creates an empty set; `addInitialConditionEntry(project, id, path, value, unit)` fills it. As with parameter entries, one call can add several entries: give each field as a vector with one element per entry, all of the same length.

| Field | Required | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | **yes** | non-empty strings, one per entry | Molecule path in OSPS notation. |
| `value` | **yes** | numbers, one per entry | |
| `unit` | **yes** | non-empty strings, one per entry | Required, unlike a parameter entry's `units`. A blank unit is rejected at run time, so it is rejected when you write it instead. |

Every field here is required, so nothing falls back to the model file.

## Output path

`addOutputPath(project, id, path)`.

| Field | Required | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | **yes** | non-empty string | The full model path in OSPS notation. |

The one field is required, so nothing falls back to the model file. An empty path value is a critical error. Two ids pointing at the same path is a warning, not an error, since sharing an output between scenarios is legitimate.

## Observed data

`addObservedData(project, entry)`, where `entry` is either a configuration list or a `DataSet` object. Unlike the other `add*` functions this one is not vectorized over ids: it adds one source per call.

Required fields by `type`:

| `type` | Required fields | Reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `excel` | `file`, `importerConfiguration`, `sheets` | Sheets of a workbook through an OSPS data-importer configuration. |
| `pkml` | `file` | A `DataSet` saved to a PKML file. |
| `script` | `file` | An R script returning a `DataSet` or a list of them. |
| `programmatic` | none | A `DataSet` built in the session. |

| Field | Required | Type | If omitted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | **yes** | one of the four above | Critical error. |
| `file` | per type | string | Critical error for `excel`, `pkml`, `script`. Relative to the project's data folder. |
| `importerConfiguration` | `excel` only | string | Critical error for an `excel` source. |
| `sheets` | `excel` only | character vector | Critical error for an `excel` source. An empty but present `sheets` counts as missing. |
| `id` | no | string | Inherited from the source: the file basename for a file-based source, the `DataSet` name for an unsaved programmatic one. |

A file that does not exist on disk is a warning rather than an error, so a project whose data lives elsewhere still loads. A path that escapes the data folder is a critical error, matching the abort the loader raises.

Observed-data ids are matched **verbatim**, not canonicalized like every other definition kind. A saved programmatic source changes its id: `saveProject()` writes the `DataSet` to `<name>.pkml` and rewrites the entry as a `pkml` source, so afterwards you remove it by that file basename rather than by the original `DataSet` name.

The source id and the DataSet name are different names; `vignette("about-the-plotting-model")` explains why. Read the DataSet name from `getObservedDataNames()`.

## DataCombined

`addDataCombined(project, id, simulated = list(), observed = list())`. Both arguments are lists of entry lists.

A `simulated` entry:

| Field | Required | Type | If omitted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | no | string | The curve is named by whatever is written in `path`. |
| `scenario` | **yes** | id | Critical error. |
| `path` | **yes** | string | Critical error. An output-path id, or a full model path used verbatim when it matches no id. An id is matched the way the project's other references are matched, so its spelling need not be the canonical one: `Aciclovir_PVB` finds `aciclovir_pvb`. |
| `group` | no | string | The curve is not grouped. Curves sharing a group are plotted together. |

An `observed` entry:

| Field | Required | Type | If omitted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | **yes** | string | Critical error. |
| `dataSet` | **yes** | DataSet name | Critical error. This is the DataSet name, not the observed-data source id. Read it from `getObservedDataNames(project)`. |
| `group` | no | string | The curve is not grouped. |

`label` is required on an observed entry: DataSet names are long, so a name taken from the data would read worse in the legend than the one you write.

The labels of the curves in one DataCombined must be distinct, counting the labels you write and the ones taken from `path`, and counting simulated and observed curves together. A repeated label is a critical error, and plotting stops rather than dropping one of the two curves. The same label may be used again in another DataCombined.

Optional per-curve transforms, applied before plotting. An offset requires its unit field:

| Field | Type | If omitted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xOffsets` | numeric | No offset on x. Requires `xOffsetsUnits`. |
| `xOffsetsUnits` | string | Aborts when `xOffsets` is given. |
| `yOffsets` | numeric | No offset on y. Requires `yOffsetsUnits`. |
| `yOffsetsUnits` | string | Aborts when `yOffsets` is given. |
| `xScaleFactors` | numeric | No scaling, factor `1`. |
| `yScaleFactors` | numeric | No scaling, factor `1`. |

## Plot

`addPlot(project, id, dataCombined, plotType, ...)`. Both `dataCombined` and `plotType` are required.

| Field | Required | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dataCombined` | **yes** | id | Must reference a known DataCombined. |
| `plotType` | **yes** | one of the five below | An unknown value is a critical error. |

### Plot types

| `plotType` | Draws |
| --- | --- |
| `individual` | A time profile for an individual scenario. |
| `population` | A time profile for a population scenario. |
| `observedVsSimulated` | Simulated against observed values. |
| `residualsVsSimulated` | Residuals against simulated values. |
| `residualsVsTime` | Residuals against time. |

### Configuration fields

A plot accepts the plot settings of esqlabsR 5.x under the same names, plus five fields of its own (`aggregation`, `quantiles`, `nsd`, `foldDistance`, `lloqOnBothAxes`). Pass them through `...` of `addPlot()`, or as columns of the `plotConfiguration` sheet of an Excel project. **An unknown field name, or a value outside the rule of its field, is a critical validation error**, and `addPlot()` refuses it.

**Every configuration field is optional**, and none of them fall back to the model file. A field you leave out takes the ESQlabs value of `createEsqlabsPlotConfiguration()` (text sizes, line and point sizes, colors, legend position), or else the default of the OSP Suite plot function.

In the table, "time profiles" are the `individual` and `population` plots, and "residual plots" are `residualsVsSimulated` and `residualsVsTime`.

| Fields | Applies to | Value | Controls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `xUnit` | time profiles, `residualsVsTime` | A unit | Unit of the time axis |
| `yUnit` | time profiles, `observedVsSimulated`, `residualsVsSimulated` | A unit | Unit of the y values. On `observedVsSimulated` and `residualsVsSimulated` the x axis also shows y values |
| `title`, `subtitle`, `caption`, `xLabel`, `yLabel` | all | Text, used as written | Plot title, subtitle, caption, and axis titles |
| `legendTitle` | all | Text, used as written | Title of the legend of the groups |
| `<text>Color`, `<text>Size`, `<text>FontFace`, `<text>FontFamily`, `<text>Angle`, `<text>Align`, `<text>Margin`, where `<text>` is `title`, `subtitle`, `caption`, `xLabel`, `yLabel`, `legendTitle`, `legendKeys` (legend entries), `xAxisLabelTicks`, or `yAxisLabelTicks` (tick labels) | all | A color; a size in points; `"plain"`, `"bold"`, `"italic"`, or `"bold.italic"`; a font family; an angle in degrees; `"left"`, `"center"`, or `"right"`; four numbers (top, right, bottom, left, in points) | Look of that text |
| `legendPosition` | all | `"none"`, `"insideTop"`, `"insideTopLeft"`, `"insideLeft"`, `"insideBottomLeft"`, `"insideBottom"`, `"insideBottomRight"`, `"insideRight"`, `"insideTopRight"`, the same eight with `outside` instead of `inside`, or `"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`, `"right"` | Legend inside the panel, or outside on the side named first and aligned toward the side named second (`"outsideTopLeft"`: above the panel, on the left) |
| `legendBackgroundColor`, `legendBackgroundAlpha`, `legendBorderColor`, `legendBorderType`, `legendBorderSize` | all | A color; 0 to 1; a color; a line type; a number | Legend box |
| `xAxisScale`, `yAxisScale` | all | `"linear"` or `"log"` | Axis scale. An `observedVsSimulated` plot has one scale for both axes, so when both fields are set they must be equal |
| `xValuesLimits`, `yValuesLimits` | all | Two numbers | Points outside are removed before drawing |
| `xAxisLimits`, `yAxisLimits` | all | Two numbers | Visible axis range; points outside are kept (zoom) |
| `xAxisTicks`, `yAxisTicks` | all | Numbers | Tick positions |
| `xAxisTicksLabels`, `yAxisTicksLabels` | all | `"default"`, `"none"`, `"identity"`, `"log"`, `"ln"`, `"sqrt"`, `"greek"`, `"pi"`, `"percentiles"`, or one text per tick | Tick labels. Texts need the ticks field with the same number of values |
| `xAxisExpand`, `yAxisExpand` | all | `TRUE` or `FALSE` | Space between the data and the panel edge |
| `xAxisColor`, `xAxisSize`, `xAxisLinetype`, and the same for `yAxis`, `xGrid`, `yGrid` | all | A color; a number; a line type | Axis lines and major grid lines |
| `plotBackgroundFill`, `plotBackgroundColor`, `plotBackgroundSize`, `plotBackgroundLinetype`, and the same for `plotPanelBackground` | all | A color; a color; a number; a line type | Background and outline of the whole plot and of the panel |
| `linesColor` | time profiles | Colors | Color of each group: curve, observed points, error bars |
| `linesSize`, `linesAlpha` | all | A number; 0 to 1 | Time profiles: the curves. `observedVsSimulated`: the fold lines. Residual plots: the zero line |
| `linesLinetype` | time profiles, residual plots | Line types | Time profiles: one line type per simulated data set. Residual plots: the zero line |
| `pointsColor` | `observedVsSimulated`, residual plots | Colors | Color of each group |
| `pointsShape`, `pointsSize`, `pointsAlpha` | all | Shape names (`"circle"`, `"diamond"`, `"triangle"`, `"square"`, ...); a number; 0 to 1 | Observed points, with one shape per observed data set |
| `ribbonsFill`, `ribbonsAlpha`, `ribbonsSize`, `ribbonsLinetype` | `population` | Colors; 0 to 1; a number; a line type | Percentile or standard deviation band. Setting the size or line type draws the band outline |
| `errorbarsSize`, `errorbarsCapSize`, `errorbarsLinetype`, `errorbarsAlpha` | time profiles, `observedVsSimulated` | A number; a number; a line type; 0 to 1 | Error bars of observed data |
| `lloqDirection` | time profiles, `observedVsSimulated` | Time profiles: `"horizontal"`. `observedVsSimulated`: `"vertical"` or `"both"` | Where the LLOQ is drawn |
| `lloqOnBothAxes` | `observedVsSimulated` | `TRUE` or `FALSE` | LLOQ on both axes (default `TRUE`) |
| `foldDistance` | `observedVsSimulated` | Numbers | Fold lines around the line of identity |
| `foldLinesLegend` | `observedVsSimulated` | `TRUE` or `FALSE` | `FALSE` leaves the fold lines out of the legend |
| `aggregation`, `quantiles`, `nsd` | `population` | How the population is summarized. `quantiles` is three probabilities | Percentile or standard deviation band |

A color is a color name (`"red"`) or a hexadecimal code (`"#4ABDCB"`). A line type is `"blank"`, `"solid"`, `"dashed"`, `"dotted"`, `"dotdash"`, `"longdash"`, `"twodash"`, or a number from 0 to 6 in that order. Fields with several values use them in order and start again when there are more groups or data sets than values.

Some rules where fields act on the same thing:

- **Colors on time profiles.** A simulated curve and its observed points share one group color, set by `linesColor`. `pointsColor` applies only to `observedVsSimulated` and residual plots. On a `population` plot the band takes `ribbonsFill`.
- **Limits.** When value limits and axis limits are both set on one axis, the axis limits set the visible range and the points outside the value limits are removed.
- **LLOQ.** `lloqDirection` and `lloqOnBothAxes` must agree on an `observedVsSimulated` plot. A direction the plot type cannot draw is a critical error.

A field with several values is stored as one comma-separated string (`"0, 12, 24"`), which is also what `addPlot()` stores for a vector. A value that contains a comma is put in double quotes (`"\"12 h, second dose\", end"`). Text fields such as `title` are never split.

Validation warns about a field that has no effect: a field set on a plot type it does not apply to, and a text style field without its text (`titleColor` without `title`).

### Settings the OSP Suite cannot draw yet

A plot accepts these esqlabsR 5.x settings, so a project or workbook that uses them still loads, but they have no effect: the OSP Suite plot functions have no option for them yet. Validation warns when a plot sets one.

- `watermark`, `watermarkColor`, `watermarkSize`, `watermarkFontFace`, `watermarkFontFamily`, `watermarkAngle`, `watermarkAlign`, `watermarkMargin`: a watermark on one plot. To mark all figures of a session, use the `{ospsuite.plots}` watermark: `options(ospsuite.plots.watermarkEnabled = TRUE)`.
- `displayLLOQ`: a plot without the lower limit of quantification.
- `foldLinesLegendDiagonal`: the fold-line legend without the line of identity.
- `linesLinetype` on an `observedVsSimulated` plot: the line types of the fold lines.

## Plot grid

`addPlotGrid(project, id, plots, ...)`.

| Field | Required | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plots` | **yes** | character vector of plot ids | Stored as one comma-separated string. Every plot listed becomes a panel. |

`plots` is required, so nothing falls back to the model file. `...` accepts grid fields such as `title` and `subtitle`, and a grid without them is drawn untitled.

## Parameter identification

`addPITask(project, id, scenarios, parameters, outputMappings, configuration)`.

| Field | Required to create | Required to run | Type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scenarios` | no | **yes** | character vector of scenario ids |
| `parameters` | no | **yes** | list of PI Parameter records |
| `outputMappings` | no | **yes** | list of PI Output Mapping records |
| `configuration` | no | no | list (algorithm, confidence-interval method, and similar) |

Leaving `configuration` out uses the runtime's own optimization defaults. A task can be created empty and filled in afterwards, but an empty task cannot run: validation reports a missing `scenarios`, `parameters`, or `outputMappings` as a critical error, and the run gates on validation.

Removing the last parameter and the last mapping leaves nothing to fit, so the now-empty task is removed for you, with a warning saying so.

### PI parameter

`addPIParameter(project, task, path, scenarios, minValue, maxValue, startValue, units = NULL, id = NULL)`.

| Field | Required | Type | If omitted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | **yes** | string | Aborts. Model parameter path to estimate. |
| `scenarios` | **yes** | character vector of ids | Aborts. |
| `minValue` | **yes** | numeric | Aborts. Lower bound. |
| `maxValue` | **yes** | numeric | Aborts. Upper bound. |
| `startValue` | **yes** | numeric | Aborts. Starting value. |
| `units` | no | string | The parameter's own unit. |
| `id` | no | string | Auto-generated. |

### PI output mapping

`addPIOutputMapping(project, task, outputPath, observedData, scenarios, ...)`.

| Field | Required | Type | If omitted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `outputPath` | **yes** | output-path id | Aborts. |
| `observedData` | **yes** | observed-data name | Aborts. |
| `scenarios` | **yes** | character vector of ids | Aborts. |
| `scaling` | no | `"lin"` or `"log"` | The runtime default. |
| `xOffset` | no | numeric | `0`. |
| `yOffset` | no | numeric | `0`. |
| `xFactor` | no | numeric | `1`. |
| `yFactor` | no | numeric | `1`. |
| `weight` | no | numeric scalar or vector | The data is unweighted. |
| `id` | no | string | Auto-generated as `<task>_mapping_<N>`. |

A build error (an unknown parameter path, output, or observed dataset) fails hard and stops the call, so a typo surfaces immediately. A numerical failure in the optimization leaves that task's `result` as `NULL` with an `error` element, and the remaining tasks still run.

## Creating several definitions in one call

Most `add*` functions are **vectorized over the id**: pass a vector of ids to add several definitions at once.

| Argument shape | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| The `id` vector | Sets the count, N. |
| A scalar field | Recycled to all N. |
| A length-N vector | Aligned to the ids by position, one value per definition. |
| A field that is itself a vector for one definition (such as `parameterSets`) | Applied whole to each definition. |

The call is **all-or-nothing**: if any one definition fails validation, none is applied.

The plot functions carry two asymmetries worth knowing, because they are the places the rules above do not read the way you would guess.

**A `...` field is applied whole, not split.** A length-N atomic vector passed through `...` is treated as one multi-value field and collapsed to a comma-separated string, so `title = c("A", "B")` gives every plot the single title `"A, B"`. To vary a `...` field per definition, pass a length-N **list**: `title = list("A", "B")`.

**`plots` in `addPlotGrid()` is whole-per-grid.** `dataCombined` and `plotType` in `addPlot()` align by position as usual, but a bare character vector passed to `plots` is applied intact to every grid, since a grid normally holds several plots. Only a length-N **list** assigns per grid:

```r
# Both grids get both plots:
addPlotGrid(project, c("g1", "g2"), plots = c("p1", "p2"))

# g1 gets p1, g2 gets p2:
addPlotGrid(project, c("g1", "g2"), plots = list("p1", "p2"))
```

`addObservedData()` is not vectorized at all: its second argument is an entry, not an id.

## Sensitivity plot configuration

The three sensitivity plotting functions each recognize a subset of `defaultPlotConfiguration` fields, because each has a different visual structure. A plot configuration field the function does not recognize has no effect. A name that is not a plot configuration field (a misspelling such as `lineColour`) stops the function with an error.

| Configuration field | `sensitivitySpiderPlot()` | `sensitivityTimeProfiles()` | `sensitivityTornadoPlot()` | Controls |
| --- | :-: | :-: | :-: | --- |
| `legendPosition` | yes | yes | yes | Legend placement |
| `legendTitle` | yes | yes | yes | Legend title |
| `linesAlpha` | yes | yes | | Line transparency |
| `linesColor` | yes | yes | yes | Line colour, or bar colour for the tornado |
| `linesSize` | yes | yes | | Line thickness |
| `pointsShape` | yes | yes | | Point shape |
| `pointsSize` | yes | | | Point size |
| `title` | yes | yes | yes | Main title |
| `titleSize` | yes | yes | yes | Title font size |
| `subtitle` | yes | | yes | Subtitle |
| `xAxisScale` | yes | yes | | X-axis scale, `"log"` or `"linear"` |
| `xLabel` | yes | yes | yes | X-axis label |
| `xValuesLimits` | yes | | | X-value limits |
| `yAxisScale` | yes | yes | | Y-axis scale, `"log"` or `"linear"` |
| `yAxisTicks` | yes | | | Y-axis tick count |
| `yAxisLimits` | yes | | | Y-axis limits |
| `yValuesLimits` | yes | | | Y-value limits |
| `yLabel` | yes | yes | yes | Y-axis label |

A setting that still has its ESQlabs value is replaced by the function's own value. For example, the ESQlabs `legendPosition` is `"outsideTopLeft"`, and the spider plot and the time profiles put the legend at the bottom and the tornado plot on the right. A value you change is kept. The sensitivity plots accept the `legendPosition` values `"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`, `"right"`, and `"none"`.

Some settings are also exposed as direct function arguments, such as `xAxisScale` and `yAxisScale` on `sensitivityTimeProfiles()` and `xAxisType` and `yAxisType` on `sensitivitySpiderPlot()`. A direct argument **overrides** the configuration object, which is the mechanism for a one-off change without editing the configuration.

`createEsqlabsPlotConfiguration()` returns a named list that holds the ESQlabs values of these fields. Change an entry with `$`, for example `myConfiguration$linesSize <- 1`. The plots themselves are drawn with `{ggplot2}`; the OSP Suite plot functions used by `createPlots()` come from [`{ospsuite.plots}`](https://www.open-systems-pharmacology.org/OSPSuite.Plots/).
